routing_reason: Existing Stripe Billing source update: full new raw + matched prior raw + current source; preserve version, UI variant, client/server, state and dated evidence boundaries; no semantic assumptions from collection diff alone.
findings: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/paypal is a 14-line variant index only (new 5-14). It identifies Stripe-hosted and Direct API routes but contains no setup, eligibility, billing-agreement, off_session, mandate, payment, or subscription-status instructions. The collection diff deletes May body text as a rendering/variant change, not evidence of deprecation or changed behavior. Do not add this navigation-only capture to factual raw_files.

The matched May capture contains two different integration surfaces: Checkout Session creation on the server and buyer redirect in the Stripe-hosted path (old 8-20,89-174), and a server-created SetupIntent plus client-side `stripe.confirmPayPalSetup`, webhook confirmation, then server-side subscription creation in the Direct API path (old 620-629,649-662,695-796,798-842). The buyer's PayPal account, Stripe customer-configured Account v2 or Customer v1, SetupIntent, PaymentMethod, Mandate and Subscription are separate identities/states.

Hosted recurring enablement is described as automatic for most activated users with possible manual enablement due to PayPal regional restrictions (old 18-20); the Direct API variant says to enable recurring payments and check specific business-location eligibility (old 626-629). Neither the old capture nor the November index verifies current account eligibility. The current source 17-18 keeps the distinction, though its summary should be explicitly dated.

Old Direct API examples for initial subscription creation pass `off_session: true` (old 809-839), and old update prose says it is needed on update to avoid another PayPal redirect for a new payment (old 848-850). However the same old guide's optional billing-anchor and trial creation examples omit `off_session` (old 909-935,951-977), so current source 13,42-46 and `wiki/concepts/stripe-paypal.md` 41,45 overstate an unqualified all-creates-and-updates requirement. This is an existing-source correction; new index 9-14 does not adjudicate requiredness.

Direct API setup authorization is not subscription payment success: old 762-796 shows PayPal billing-agreement approval and `setup_intent.succeeded`/`setup_intent.setup_failed`/`mandate.updated`; the subscription create and subsequent active status follow at old 798-846. Hosted success URL is not sufficient for fulfillment by itself (old 140-174). Detaching the saved PayPal PaymentMethod revokes the Stripe Mandate and calls PayPal to cancel the billing agreement (old 982-994), a consequential historical effect to retain with dated scope.

Root `wiki/index.md` 7 routes to `wiki/stripe-index.md` 792 `[[stripe-subscriptions]]`, which links this source at `wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md` 249. `wiki/concepts/stripe-paypal.md` 68 also reciprocally links it; its requiredness at 45 shares the source overstatement. The Stripe index does not directly list this source, but the concept route exists. No repository file was edited.
substantive_changes: No substantive PayPal subscription behavior change is established by the November index. Its only new information is explicit navigation to Stripe-hosted and Direct API variant URLs (new 9-14); the May capture already contained both variant bodies (old 8-10,620-624).

The recommended source correction concerns an old internal tension and existing summary wording, not a November behavior change: qualify `off_session=true` on Direct API creation/update to what the May prose and examples actually establish (old 809-850,909-977).
conflicts: Current source 13,42-46 and `wiki/concepts/stripe-paypal.md` 41,45 say `off_session=true` is required on all Direct API subscription creates and updates. Old guide's update instruction at 850 supports the update portion, and initial create examples at 809-839 show the flag, but optional create examples at 909-935 and 951-977 omit it. The captured material does not support an unqualified universal-create rule; qualify and cross-link the discrepancy.

Current source 50-53 says the Mandate contains `payer_email`, `payer_id` and `billing_agreement_id`. Old 786 says Mandate payment_method_details contains payer ID and billing-agreement ID while buyer email and payer ID can also be found on PaymentMethod.paypal; old 788-792 table lacks an explicit owner. Avoid a blanket Mandate-field ownership claim and retain exact object paths.

The concept labels Checkout recommended at `wiki/concepts/stripe-paypal.md` 10,22, but this matched May guide only calls Stripe.js recommended in its Direct API setup at old 735-737. The new index makes no path preference; preserve any recommendation only with separately verified evidence.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May Stripe-hosted Checkout flow, receipt and fulfillment warning, recurring-payment Dashboard caveat, and optional feature examples as dated variant evidence (old 8-20,106-174,239-613); omission from November's index is not deprecation.

Keep the May Direct API SetupIntent/PayPal billing-agreement approval, client/server split, Account v2 versus Customer v1, authorization webhooks, PaymentMethod/Mandate identities, off_session examples and update warning as dated evidence (old 620-850), with its own example inconsistency noted.

Keep May's detachment consequence and its caveat that eligibility is limited by business location and setup (old 626-629,982-994); do not infer current eligibility, mandate state, successful charging or bank receipt from the November index.
unresolved_questions: The November variant bodies were not part of the assigned capture, so their current instructions, PayPal recurring eligibility, API/Stripe.js version support, and any changed `off_session` contract remain unresolved.

The May Direct API guide's optional subscription-create snippets omit `default_payment_method` and `off_session` even though the central create examples include both (old 809-839 versus 909-977). This could reflect abbreviated examples; the assigned evidence cannot resolve their operational validity or make an unconditional requiredness claim.
